statement: If Am,C0 contains a nonaffine member, then there exist κ ∈ (0, ∞) and v ∈ Am,C0 centered at z∗ = (0, 1) for which (5.2) holds with f = v and I = R. For t > 0 set W(x, t) = Ctv(x, t) − κ2t 2 . (5.7) This function is continuous, has subquadratic spatial growth on compact positive-time intervals, and is a viscosity subsolution of (3.1) on Rm × (0, ∞). It satisfies v(x, t) − κ2t 2 ≤ W(x, t) ≤ v(x, t) (t > 0), W(z∗) = v(z∗) = 0, (5.8) and W(·, t)−|x|2/(2t) is concave for every t > 0. At every point of contact with t > 0, the barycentric gap satisfies W(x, t) = v(x, t) =⇒ Ctv(x, t) − v(x, t) t = κ2 2 > 0. (5.9) Finally, Hv(z∗) ∈ R, lim ℓ↓0 S+ ℓ W(z∗) = Hv(z∗). (5.10)
